newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai oil firm to buy Caltex low-sulphur diesel.
newsitem.headline: Thai oil firm to buy Caltex low-sulphur diesel.

text.p: State-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) will buy 12 million litres per month of low-sulphur gas oil from Thai Oil Co Ltd and Caltex's Star Petroleum Refining Co Ltd, starting January next year, a senior PTT official said on Thursday.

Prasert Bunsumpun, president of PTT Oil, told reporters that the purchase of 0.05 percent sulphur gas oil from the two refiners is a part of PTT's procurement of oil for state-run Bangkok Mass Transit Authority of Thailand which operated bus services in the city.
He said PTT decided to buy from the two refiners because they were the only ones with the technical capability to produce 0.05 percent sulphur gas oil at the moment.
Most local refineries currently produce 0.25 percent sulphur.
Although Prasert did not elaborate on the details of purchase, he said the government will subsidise by paying PTT 16 satang per litre ($0.64) to keep BMTA's operating cost low.
But Prasert did not elaborate on the term of purchase.
Thai government required that cars use 0.05 percent diesel from 1999 but BMTA must start using the product from next year.
Thai Oil refinery, in which PTT has a majority stake, is producing 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) of refined product.
Star Petroleum refinery was a joint venture between U.S. oil firm Caltex and PTT. It has production capacity of 130,000 bpd.
